params.name: quad
params.let: 'first and third' if s == 1 else 'second and fourth'

stem: A hyperbola has the equation $y=\frac{a}{x}$. Its graph lies in the {=quad} quadrants, and it lies {=cmp} the axes than the graph of $y=\frac{{=c}}{x}$. Which of the following could be the equation of the hyperbola?
solution: The sign of $a$ decides the quadrants: if $a>0$ the graph lies in the first and third quadrants, and if $a<0$ it lies in the second and fourth quadrants. The graph lies in the {=quad} quadrants, so $a$ is {=sw}.

The size of $a$ decides how far the graph lies from the axes: the bigger $|a|$ is, the further the graph lies from the axes. The graph of $y=\frac{{=c}}{x}$ has $|a|={=c}$, and our graph must lie {=cmp} the axes than this one, so $|a|$ must be {=bs} than {=c}.
Only $y={=sg}\frac{{=m}}{x}$ has a {=sw} value of $a$ with $|a|={=m}$, which is {=bs} than {=c}. The other equations have the wrong sign of $a$ or the wrong size of $a$.
notes: The book's questions for this objective match a function to a drawn graph (figures of four labelled hyperbolas). A family cannot reuse the figure, so the same two ideas, the sign of a (quadrants) and the size of a (distance from the axes), are asked in words with q = 0. The three distractors each break exactly one clue: wrong sign (sign-of-a-ignored), wrong size (bigger-a-closer-to-axes), or both (null). The reference graph y = c/x is always in the first and third quadrants; 'further from the axes' is decided by |a| only.
